$comment: THE NAMED-RED LEDGER FOR THE EVAL SUITE. `docs:check` refuses a red committed run UNLESS every failing eval id appears here with a cause and a closing condition — and refuses a row here whose eval now passes. A red that is named, caused, and has a stated way to close is CARRIED; a red that is not is a silent failure, which is the one thing this project does not permit. This is the same doctrine as parity/receipts/v1/usable-baseline.json and corpus-reproducible.json, applied to the suite itself. It does NOT weaken the full lane: eval:record:check still re-measures row-by-row against a fresh run, so a lie about which evals fail is caught there.
rule: reds[].id must equal an eval id whose committed row has pass:false. cause: why it fails, measured not guessed. closesWhen: the specific event that makes it pass — not 'when fixed'. A row is deleted the moment its eval goes green; the gate refuses a stale row rather than letting it rot.

reds.cause: STALE LITERAL RECEIPT, and the ack is the stale artifact — not the engine. `examples/astryx/tokens/reanchor-decisions.json` carries an owner-acked no-match row `RA-nomatch-0536591a` for the leaf `imported.badge.root.background-color.neutral`, acked against the value `#0536591a`. That leaf is now `#e5e5e5`, so --propose refuses rather than reuse an ack recorded against a value that no longer exists. MEASURED, and it inverts the obvious reading: the CAPTURE (extract/computed/out/astryx/badge/captured-truth.json) reads `rgba(229, 229, 229, 1)` = #e5e5e5 on origin/main AND on this branch — identical bytes — so main's minted #0536591a is the value that disagrees with main's own capture, and this branch's #e5e5e5 is faithful to what the browser rendered. The ack's whole argument is an ALPHA-SERIALISATION near-miss on the authored `rgba(5, 54, 89, 0.1)`; that argument does not describe an opaque light grey, so the premise is falsified, not merely out of date. Re-acking it here would launder a false premise, and the ack note already reads 'flagged for owner review'.
reds.closesWhen: `npx tsx examples/astryx/scripts/reanchor-minted.ts --propose` is re-run AND the regenerated no-match row for `imported.badge.root.background-color.neutral` is re-reviewed by the owner against the CURRENT value — either re-acked as a no-match against #e5e5e5, or resolved to a candidate and applied. CHECKABLE WITHOUT JUDGEMENT: the acked `value` on row `RA-nomatch-0536591a` in examples/astryx/tokens/reanchor-decisions.json equals the `$value` of `imported.badge.root.background-color.neutral` in examples/astryx/tokens/astryx-minted.dtcg.json. A future round can compare those two fields. Requires an owner decision (OWNER DELEGATION does not extend to re-acking a premise that has been shown false), so no branch closes this alone.

reds.cause: The decrease-only ratchet on unreferenced minted leaves is exceeded by two libraries, and the two halves have DIFFERENT causes. astryx 8 -> 21: the 15 new leaves are astryx Badge's five STATUS variants — `imported.badge.root.background-color.{error,info,neutral,success,warning}` and their `color` twins — minted but bound by nothing, because the committed examples/astryx/contracts/badge.contract.json binds only the NINE colour variants (blue, cyan, green, orange, pink, purple, red, teal, yellow) while the FUSION OUTPUT extract/computed/out/astryx/badge/enriched.contract.json binds ALL FOURTEEN — byte-identically on origin/main and here. The engine is not at fault; the promoted contract is behind what the engine produces, which is docs/23 SS-B.37. carbon 92 -> 94: exactly two leaves, `imported.text-input.text-input.outline-width-state-active` and `...-state-focus-visible`. Neither the fusion output nor the contract binds them and neither exists on origin/main's minted set at all — the mint records a state-plane fact that `Part.states` has no vocabulary to bind, so nothing can reference it.
reds.closesWhen: BOTH halves return to or below their committed baselines (astryx <= 8, carbon <= 92) and the eval goes green — it is one row because the ratchet is one assertion. astryx half: a re-promote of the astryx half that makes badge.contract.json bind all 14 variants, matching enriched.contract.json; the 15 leaves then have referents and astryx's unreferenced count falls to 8. CHECKABLE: badge.contract.json contains an `imported.badge.root.background-color.<v>` reference for each of the five status values, and `npm run eval -- --only minted-leaves-bind-to-something` reports astryx 8. carbon half: `Part.states` gains a spelling for `outline-width` (so the two leaves acquire a binding), OR the mint stops minting a channel no binding vocabulary can express (so they are never created). Either returns carbon to 92. NOT closed by re-recording extract/computed/minted-orphan-baseline.json — the ratchet is decrease-only by design and the burn-down already declined to re-record carbon 92 -> 94.

reds.cause: The LIVE FIGMA CANVAS is the stale side, not the code. parity/receipts/console-loop/astryx/canvas-drift/LIVE-SNAPSHOT.json records the real file as it stood at its own `mintedAt: 2026-08-09`; the astryx emit scripts have been re-derived several times since and are byte-fresh against a rebuild (npm run figma:fresh, 9/9 libraries, 0 named holes). MEASURED on this tree: 3 of 13 stems in-sync, 10 DRIFT, and the drift classes are exactly what a stale canvas looks like — BINDING-DRIFT on banner, button, progress-bar, slider, text-input and token (the spec binds a channel to a variable; the live cell holds a literal), VALUE-DRIFT on checkbox-input and switch, FC-FONT-STYLE-UNRESOLVED on card and toast. The probe is the only instrument that asks whether the live cell is the product of this lane's own committed emit script, so its red is the instrument working.
reds.closesWhen: The astryx emit scripts (examples/astryx/figma/*.figma.js) are APPLIED to the live Figma file and the snapshot is RE-MINTED from it, giving parity/receipts/console-loop/astryx/canvas-drift/LIVE-SNAPSHOT.json a `mintedAt` later than the commit that last re-emitted those scripts. CHECKABLE: after the re-mint, `node scripts/console-loop-canvas-drift-probe.mjs astryx --json` reports 12 in-sync / 0 cell-pending, which is the expectation evals/run.ts already pins for astryx. Requires a FIGMA_TOKEN and write access to the live file, so no branch and no CI lane can close it — it is a human operation on the canvas.

reds.cause: MEASURED: `promoteFloor` re-promotes mui from its committed capture record into a scratch dir and byte-compares; contracts/tabs.anchors.json, tabs.contract.json, tabs.extension.json, tokens/MINTED.md and tokens/mui-minted.dtcg.json differ from the committed bytes. The mui tabs capture record changed at 48e68f107 (2026-09-01, the content remints) and the committed promotion was not re-run; the corpus gate names the same divergence in parity/receipts/v1/corpus-reproducible.json → promote.mui. Nothing in the promoter changed; the input did.
reds.closesWhen: the owner re-promotes mui from its committed capture record (the documented chain) and commits the five artifacts, or reverts the tabs capture record to the bytes the committed promotion was made from — either makes the byte-compare pass and this row is deleted.

reds.cause: The eval runs `parity/diagnose.ts extract/pilots/shoelace/extract.config.json` inside the eval's scratch copy and refuses when any finding carries surface "code". It fails in CI's full lane and in the readiness run; a direct run of the same diagnose in the working tree reports 260 findings and ZERO on the code surface (its only delta from the committed report is the hand-saved design.json's file-mtime age, a design-surface finding). Which code-surface finding the scratch copy produces is NOT established here; no commit since the last green record (9553a6a56) touched extract/pilots/shoelace, parity/diagnose.ts or core/. Recorded as failing rather than as the pass it carried on 2026-09-01.
reds.closesWhen: the scratch-copy diagnose is run with its report kept (evals/.scratch/extract/pilots/shoelace/out/diagnose-report.json) and the code-surface finding is read, then either the pilot's code surface is fixed or the finding is shown to be the scratch copy's own artefact — the eval goes green and this row is deleted.
